title: NATO allies agree 5 percent of GDP defence spending target at The Hague summit
body:
At the NATO summit in The Hague, Netherlands, in late June 2025, allies agreed to devote 5 percent of GDP to defence by 2035. Of this, 3.5 percent is for core defence spending and 1.5 percent for related areas such as infrastructure, civil preparedness and support for Ukraine. The declaration refers to a review in 2029. The 2014 Wales pledge had set a goal of 2 percent for 2024, and some members still had not met it.

Spain objected that the new target was unrealistic and did not receive a formal opt-out. Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty noted that the final wording says allies "commit to invest 5%," which may give some flexibility in interpretation.

The declaration was the shortest summit statement on record. It names Russia a "long-term threat" to Euro-Atlantic security and reaffirms Article 5, the alliance's mutual defence clause. US President Donald Trump said "there are numerous definitions of Article 5," which alarmed European diplomats, and he later said the United States was with its allies "all the way."

On Ukraine, the declaration contains no language on membership, and there was no NATO-Ukraine Council meeting. Its only mention of Ukraine concerns sovereign support and defence-industry contributions counting toward allies' spending. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte offered heavy praise to Trump, crediting him for increased European defence spending, which helped the declaration pass smoothly.
